body.content: Contradiction: If we define 'reliability' as the ability to produce the correct outcome consistently, then 'mere checklist compliance' that tracks the right answer IS a reliability gain. Why does the prompt distinguish 'genuine reliability' from 'compliance that happens to track the right answer'? This implies a distinction between 'Robustness' (the process works because it understands the problem) and 'Luck/Coincidence' (the process works because the checklist was lucky).
body.why_keep_this: Challenges the premise of the second half of the problem prompt.
